import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Standardize the breed names to handle potential inconsistencies
df['Rasse1Text'] = df['Rasse1Text'].str.strip()

# Identify the top 10 most common breeds across all years
top_10_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# Filter the DataFrame to include only the top 10 breeds
df_top_breeds = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_10_breeds)].copy()

# Group by year and breed, then count the number of registrations
breed_trends = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'Rasse1Text']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# Determine the year range for the title
min_year = breed_trends['StichtagDatJahr'].min()
max_year = breed_trends['StichtagDatJahr'].max()

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 9))

# Generate a color palette with enough colors for the top 10 breeds
palette = sns.color_palette("tab10", n_colors=10)

# Create the line plot showing trends for each breed
sns.lineplot(
    data=breed_trends,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='count',
    hue='Rasse1Text',
    hue_order=top_10_breeds, # Keep consistent color mapping
    palette=palette,
    marker='o',
    linewidth=2.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---

# Set a clear and informative title
ax.set_title(
    f'Popularity Trends of Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich ({min_year}-{max_year})',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=20
)

# Label the axes
ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=14)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=14)

# Improve tick formatting
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True)) # Ensure x-axis ticks are integers
plt.xticks(rotation=0)

# Enhance the legend and move it outside the plot area
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(
    handles=handles,
    labels=labels,
    title='Dog Breed',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=11,
    title_fontsize=13
)

# Add a subtle grid for better readability
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.7)
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.5)

# Remove top and right spines for a cleaner look
sns.despine(ax=ax)

# Adjust layout to ensure everything fits, especially the external legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
